role.altitude: The technical director keeps the talks between engineering, production and promotions, the shoots and the policy choices; request chasing, booking checks, promo versioning and status mails shrink.
skills_to_grow: Running requests, bookings and file checks on rules in shared systems
role.ambitious_version: A technical director whose studios and edit suites book themselves within rules, with time spent on the hard technical calls.

tasks.short: Join production meetings, take technical requests from producers, clarify them, turn them into engineering work orders, settle issues between engineering and production, and report status back.

steps.what: Technical director acts as liaison in production meetings, learning the technical needs of upcoming programmes
Producers send their technical needs (equipment, crew, feeds) by mail
Technical director collects and clarifies the technical requirements per production
Technical director turns the requirements into engineering work orders and assigns engineers
Technical director settles technical issues and conflicts between engineering and production departments
Technical director reports the status of technical work back to production by mail

tasks.design: Producers submit technical needs through a request form on the {WORKFLOW} platform with required fields (date, studio, cameras, feeds, crew), with about the effort of a mail. Accepted requests create engineering work orders with those fields, which the technical director assigns, and the status of each order shows on the request, so producers see progress without mail. Production meetings and settling issues stay with the technical director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived as free mails with missing details, and work orders were retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Low-code request forms create work orders and show status to the requester.
tasks.still_hard: Departments with different priorities for the same engineers.
tasks.human_edge: Translating what a producer wants into what engineering can deliver.
tasks.altitude: Less mail; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether structured requests cut call-backs to producers.

evidence.claim: Low-code platforms turn form submissions into work orders and show their status to the requester.

assumptions: Boundary: from production meetings to status reported; the engineering work itself is outside.
Input contract for s3: request form fields filled by producers (s2); fallback is the technical director entering mail requests.
Coverage: about 80% of requests come through the form; s3 is priced at that share.
Producers' form time is about that of a mail, shown in s2 and outside the technical director's savings.
Meetings and settling issues keep their full time.
research_questions: How many requests need a call-back before and after the form?

already_counted.description: Technical director enters mail requests from producers who skip the form.

incremental.description: Technical director keeps form fields and work order types current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few large productions with long meetings; high: many small productions sending frequent requests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree promo concepts with the promotions director, plan crew, studio and edit time, supervise the shoot, oversee editing and versions, check files, get approval and deliver promos to playout.

steps.what: Technical director collaborates with the promotions director on promo concepts and technical feasibility
Technical director plans crew, studio, graphics and edit time for the promos
Technical director supervises the shoot or recording of on-air station promotions
Technical director oversees editing, graphics and the length and date versions of each promo
Technical director checks the technical quality of each promo file
Promotions director watches the final promo versions and approves them
Technical director delivers the approved promos to the playout and traffic system

approvals.approved_version: promo versions as approved in s6, identified by file name and checksum; any re-export voids the approval

tasks.design: Crew, studio and edit time for promos are booked in the facilities booking system instead of a spreadsheet. Length and date versions (for example 30, 20 and 10 seconds with different end boards) are rendered from templates in the graphics system ({OTHER}) instead of cut one by one, and an automatic file check flags loudness and format problems. Concepts, the shoot and editing choices stay with people; only the versions the promotions director approves go to playout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each promo version was cut and checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Graphics systems render template versions; file checks run automatically.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a strong promo out of a short studio slot.
tasks.altitude: Less time on versions and checks; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether more versions per promo change how often it airs.

evidence.claim: Broadcast graphics systems render several length and date versions from one template.

assumptions: Boundary: from the promo concept to promos delivered to playout; scheduling promos is outside.
Input contract for s4: version templates with end boards and air dates set up once per campaign; fallback is cutting each version.
Concept talks and the shoot keep their full time; the promotions director's review is outside the technical director's savings.
research_questions: How many promo files fail the automatic check?

already_counted.description: Technical director checks rendered versions and flagged file issues.

incremental.description: Technical director sets up version templates per campaign.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one promo with a single version; high: a campaign with many length and date versions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect incidents and standards, confer with operations directors on technical policies, write the policy, get it approved, publish it, brief staff and check compliance.

steps.what: Technical director collects incidents, faults and delivery standards that call for a policy
Technical director confers with operations directors to formulate fair and attainable technical policies
Technical director writes the technical policy and delivery specification

loop.input: The agreed policy points and the register of technical standards with limit values.
loop.output: Draft policy sections in the house format.
loop.check: Every limit value must match the standards register, or it is marked; points not agreed in s2 are removed; the technical director edits every section.
loop.stop: One draft per version of agreed points; if rejected, the technical director writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives headings; each rule needs wording staff can follow.

steps.what: Operations director reviews the final policy and approves it
Technical director publishes the approved policy on the intranet
Technical director briefs producers and engineers on the policy
Technical director maintains the policies by checking compliance from file check and incident records

approvals.approved_version: technical policy as approved by the operations director in s4; any edit after approval needs a new approval

tasks.design: A dashboard on the incident tickets in {HELPDESK} and the automatic file check results shows faults by type and producer, so policy issues and later compliance are read, not compiled. A bounded step drafts policy sections from the agreed points with every limit value checked against the standards register; the technical director edits, the operations director approves, and only that version is published. Conferring and briefing stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents and file problems were compiled by hand before each policy talk.
tasks.enabler_now: Ticket systems and file checks hold faults as data; language models draft text checked against a register.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing a rule that is fair to busy producers and still protects the air.
tasks.human_edge: Getting producers to accept a rule they find a burden.
tasks.altitude: Policy talks start from data; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which faults keep recurring after a policy change.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft policy text whose limit values can be checked against a standards register.
Fault counts per producer must not be used to rate staff without works council consent under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from policy issues to compliance review; enforcement is outside.
Input contract for s1 and s7: incident tickets with category from the helpdesk and file check results from the media system; fallback is collecting by hand.
Fault data is used for policies, not to judge individuals.
Conferring, approval and briefing keep their full time.
research_questions: Do faults fall after a policy is published?

already_counted.description: Technical director edits drafted policy sections.

incremental.description: Technical director keeps the standards register current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small policy change agreed in one meeting; high: a new delivery specification with many limits and a compliance follow-up.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take requests for studio and editing facilities, check availability and clashes, decide priorities, plan maintenance windows, confirm bookings, handle changes and report actual use for cost allocation.

steps.what: Producers and engineers ask for studio and edit time by mail or phone
Technical director checks availability and clashes in the facilities spreadsheet and accepts bookings
Technical director decides priorities when requests for studio and editing facilities clash
Technical director schedules maintenance windows with engineering and maintenance staff
Technical director confirms bookings to the requesters
Technical director handles last-minute changes and overruns
Technical director reports facility use per production for cost allocation

approvals.approved_version: booking as accepted by the technical director in s2 (facility, date, times, production); a change makes a new booking that needs a new acceptance

tasks.design: A facilities booking system ({OTHER}) replaces the spreadsheet: producers and engineers request studio and edit time in it, it shows availability and blocks double bookings, and maintenance windows are recurring blocks. The technical director accepts each booking, which sends the confirmation, and decides priorities when requests clash. Users check in and out on a panel at each studio and suite, so the use report for cost allocation shows actual times, not booked ones.
tasks.previous_blocker: One spreadsheet and many mails held all bookings, so every request meant checking by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Room and resource booking systems with rules and check-in panels are standard configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which production gets the studio when both are urgent.
tasks.human_edge: Fair priorities that keep producers and engineers on side.
tasks.altitude: Most booking admin goes; the technical director decides clashes and changes.

reach.learn: How far actual use differs from booked time.

evidence.claim: Resource booking systems block double bookings, send confirmations and record check-in and check-out times.
Check-in records show who used a studio when; using them to monitor staff needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from facility requests to the use report; the productions and maintenance work are outside.
Input contract for s7: actual start and end times from check-in panels, produced by the users at each studio and suite; booked times are the fallback where no check-in is recorded.
Requesters enter bookings with about the effort of today's mails (s1); checking in and out is new work for them, counted as other-role upkeep.
Priority decisions keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of studios and suites and bookings per week.
Whether costs are allocated per production today.
research_questions: How often does actual use differ from the booking?

already_counted.description: Technical director reviews booking requests the system flags as clashing or outside rules.
Technical director checks missing check-ins before the use report goes out.

incremental.description: Technical director keeps facilities, rules and maintenance blocks current.
Producers and engineers check in and out at the studio panel.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: two studios with stable weekly bookings; high: many studios and edit suites with daily requests and changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
